content.scenario: A consumer files an application with the District Commission to review an order passed against them, citing an error apparent on the face of the record. The consumer claims that the order was passed without considering crucial evidence.
content.outcome: The District Commission reviews the order and finds that there was indeed an error apparent on the face of the record. The Commission passes a revised order, taking into account the new evidence and correcting the earlier mistake.

keywords: error apparent on the face of the record
user_queries: How can a consumer review an order passed by the District Commission?
